udt_struct_v0.doc: One anchored commitment: the content hash it binds and the ledger sequence\nwhere the binding was first recorded.
udt_struct_v0.name: Anchor

udt_error_enum_v0.doc: Fail-closed error codes (never invent a success).
udt_error_enum_v0.name: CgError

cases.doc: The stored record's owner does not equal the one under verification.\nUnreachable without a SHA-256 collision on the derivation (the id\nbinds the owner); kept as an explicit dead-man's-say to stay fail-closed.
cases.name: OwnerMismatch

udt_struct_v0.doc: One AUTHORIZED anchor: adds the identity of the owner whose signature the\nwrite required, so a read-back can prove WHO anchored the commitment.
udt_struct_v0.name: AuthorizedAnchor

function_v0.doc: Read an anchor: None when the id was never anchored.
function_v0.name: read

function_v0.doc:
Anchor a commitment id -> content hash at this ledger sequence.
Public: anyone may anchor; authority lives with the caller's policy.
First write wins; same (id, hash) replays idemtently; a different hash
for the same id fails with HashMismatch (never overwritten).
Pre-registration race documented honestly above: this lane is the
demo/proof peer; identity-bearing callers use `commit_authorized`.
function_v0.name: commit

function_v0.doc: Version constant as an on-ledger String.
function_v0.name: version

function_v0.doc: The authorized lane's domain separator as an on-ledger String, so a\nthird party can read the exact derivation prefix from the ledger\nitself instead of trusting a source file.
function_v0.name: auth_domain

function_v0.doc: Strict read: the anchor must exist and its hash must equal the caller's\nexpectation, else the invocation fails (fail-closed verification).
function_v0.name: assert_anchored

function_v0.doc: Read an authorized anchor: None when never anchored. Returns the\nowner identity too \xe2\x80\x94 transparency lane (who anchored is public).
function_v0.name: read_authorized

function_v0.doc:
AUTHORIZED anchor: id written ONLY through the owner's signature.
The id is derived from (owner, hash) in-contract (above), so the
function CHANGES the caller's id only by refusing to take one \xe2\x80\x94
there is no id argument to lie about. Fail-closed everywhere:
- missing owner authorization -> host rejects the tx (never reaches
storage),
- a record already exists with the same (owner, hash) -> idempotent
replay of the original ledger sequence,
- any other occupied-lane shape -> fail-closed error (cryptographic
dead code, kept for defense in depth).
function_v0.name: commit_authorized

function_v0.doc:
The canonical authorized-lane id, derived IN-CONTRACT:
`sha256( utf8(AUTH_DOMAIN) ++ utf8(strkey(owner)) ++ hash )`.
Exported as a public fn so a verifier can ask the ledger for the
canonical id of an (owner, hash) pair and compare it against what was
anchored \xe2\x80\x94 the derivation itself never trusts a caller's arithmetic.
function_v0.name: derive_authorized_id

function_v0.doc:
Strict AUTHORIZED read-back (public, no signature required):
the record must exist, the id must DERIVE from (owner, hash), the
stored hash must equal the caller's hash and the stored owner must
equal the caller's owner. Every failure is fail-closed.
function_v0.name: assert_anchored_authorized
